papers.title: Bidirectional links between food intake and sleep: a naturalistic mobile EEG study
papers.summary: This naturalistic study used mobile EEG and questionnaires to examine bidirectional links between sleep and food intake in healthy participants. Results indicate that the timing of meals and sleep is reciprocally associated, while sleep quality or composition showed no negative effect after large, late, or satiating last meals.

papers.title: Working memory operations emerge from dynamic changes in neural subspace geometry
papers.summary: Using M/EEG in a working memory task, the authors found that neural subspace geometry flexibly reshapes with task demands: prioritization expands subspaces while de-prioritization shrinks them, and subspaces become more orthogonal under high cognitive demands. These changes were driven by interactions between aperiodic activity and delta/theta oscillations.

papers.title: Decision Confidence Neuron in Echo State Network for Continual Evaluation of EEG Motor Imagery Classification Quality
papers.summary: The paper proposes an explicit decision-confidence readout neuron for Echo State Networks to continuously monitor confidence during decision formation. In EEG-based motor imagery classification, confidence activity increased with decision accuracy and discriminated correct from error decisions, particularly in higher-performing participants.

papers.title: tACS increases alpha burst duration in a frequency- and montage-specific manner
papers.summary: In a randomized study with 158 participants, tACS at 10 Hz over posterior regions increased alpha power by lengthening alpha burst duration, but had no effect on 6 Hz or fronto-parietal montages, nor on behavior or resting-state cognition. This shows frequency- and montage-specific effects on alpha oscillations.

papers.title: Sleep spindle state-dependent motor cortical plasticity induction by EEG-triggered ripple burst TMS
papers.summary: The study investigated sleep spindle state-dependent plasticity induction using EEG-triggered ripple burst TMS in sleeping healthy participants. Spindle-trough rTMS led to consistent long-term depression-like changes in corticospinal and sensorimotor cortical excitability, unlike other spindle states.

papers.title: Revisiting the concept that interictal implies asymptomatic: Pulse wave amplitude drops uncover autonomic responses during generalized paroxysmal fast activities.
papers.summary: This study analyzed 511 generalized paroxysmal fast activities (GPFA) during sleep in 21 epilepsy patients using polysomnography and pulse wave amplitude drops (PWAD) as an autonomic marker. It found that 40.5% of clinically silent GPFA were associated with PWAD≥30%, indicating autonomic activation, challenging the asymptomatic notion of interictal discharges.

papers.title: Silent brains isolate the heartbeat-evoked potential
papers.summary: This study used EEGs from isoelectric patients as a negative control to isolate the heartbeat-evoked potential (HEP) from cardiac artefacts. They found a significant frontocentral negative cluster in controls, suggesting that the early HEP is a distinct cortical response.

papers.title: A cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic network model linking intermittent postural control to sway-related beta-band oscillations.
papers.summary: The paper presents a closed-loop spiking neural network model of cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic circuitry and an inverted pendulum to simulate intermittent postural control. The model reproduces sway-phase-locked beta oscillations only when intermittent control is implemented, requiring intact thalamocortical and GPe-STN circuits.

papers.title: Mice and humans use ambiguous local motion to stabilize gaze
papers.summary: The authors investigated whether ambiguous local motion signals can directly drive reflexive gaze stabilization in mice and humans, using electrophysiology, modeling, and eye tracking. They found that eye movements follow local motion even when it dissociates from global object motion, indicating a conserved sensorimotor heuristic that prioritizes local cues.

papers.title: Axonal theta oscillations evoke bursting in target hippocampal subregions.
papers.summary: This study used microfluidic devices to isolate single axons between hippocampal subregions and recorded spontaneous theta oscillations in axons that were independent of spiking. Theta phase and amplitude in axons correlated with target bursting, suggesting a functional role in inter-regional communication.

papers.title: The Expression and Effects of Rev-Erbα in Different Cerebral Regions of Mice With Acute and Chronic Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This study examined the circadian regulator Rev-Erbα in acute and chronic epilepsy mouse models. Its expression was dysregulated, and activation with SR9009 reduced seizures, abnormal EEG discharge, and improved behavioral outcomes, suggesting antiepileptic and neuroprotective effects.

papers.title: Study on the regulatory effect of magnetic vestibular stimulation on visually induced motion sickness.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effect of magnetic vestibular stimulation (MVS) on visually induced motion sickness in healthy participants. Higher-intensity MVS (110% of resting motor threshold) was associated with reduced symptoms, whereas lower-intensity MVS at 90% worsened them, with exploratory EEG network changes.

papers.title: Late cross-modal biases in neural spatial representations revealed by EEG decoding.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: The study used EEG decoding to track spatial representations during an audiovisual ventriloquist task. Cross-modal biases emerged only after ~200 ms, with auditory representations biased earlier than visual, suggesting that multisensory integration occurs via late feedback processes.

papers.title: Event-Related Spectral Signatures of Prospective Memory.
papers.summary: EEG recordings during prospective memory tasks revealed distinct oscillatory signatures: PM retrieval and cue trials showed greater alpha/low beta desynchronization than ongoing trials, with task-specific theta differences. These findings suggest specific neural mechanisms underlying intention formation, retention, and retrieval.

papers.title: Controlling the Triple Network Model: Salience Network Modulatory Roles, Default Mode Dynamic Functions, and Central Executive Network Heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes evidence on the triple network model, highlighting heterogeneity and methodological inconsistencies in network definitions. The authors propose integrating temporal dynamics and geometric hypotheses, such as neural manifolds, to improve understanding of disordered cognition.

papers.title: Periodic EEG: clinical settings, in vitro models, and potential mechanisms.
papers.summary: This review examines periodic EEG complexes in pathological conditions, categorizing contexts into infections, hypoxic/ischemic events, and metabolic disorders, and discusses potential cellular mechanisms including altered excitation-inhibition, metabotropic glutamate receptor activation, and electrical coupling, with testable predictions linking these mechanisms to anticonvulsant drug responsiveness.

papers.title: Parameter-Dependent Effects of Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation on Corticospinal Excitability and Inhibitory Control.
papers.summary: This study examined effects of four transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) protocols on motor cortical excitability and inhibitory control in healthy adults, finding that intermittent and continuous theta-burst TUS produced excitatory and inhibitory MEP effects respectively, consistent with animal models, but TUS-induced facilitation did not enhance stop-signal task performance.

papers.title: Wearable Sleep and Circadian Monitoring in Intensive Care Nursing: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review assessed wearable sleep/circadian monitoring in intensive care across 61 reports. Wearables were feasible but showed variable accuracy, especially poor wake specificity in immobile patients, and they complement but cannot replace clinical assessment for sleep evaluation.

papers.title: Transcranial photobiomodulation rebalances cortical excitation/inhibition in young adults with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, transcranial photobiomodulation over right prefrontal cortex in young adults with ADHD improved working memory, increased alpha power, steepened aperiodic exponent, and enhanced neural complexity, suggesting rebalanced excitation/inhibition and normalized neural dynamics.

papers.title: The Choreography of Coupled Brains: Coordinated Movement and Multi-Scale Neural Synchrony in Musical Theater for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities
papers.summary: This pilot study using mobile EEG and hyperscanning during a musical-theater program in individuals with developmental disabilities found that performance increased high-beta/gamma power and within-brain connectivity, while between-brain synchrony was strongest with mirrored movement and scaled with movement vigor.

papers.title: Gamma and Beta Neurofeedback Training Can Improve Visual Perception With Spectral and Regional Specificity.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial, gamma and combined gamma-beta neurofeedback training improved visual perception in healthy adults. Both groups showed increased parieto-occipital gamma, while central beta increased only in the gamma-beta group, and improvements were linked to enhanced evidence accumulation.

papers.title: Exploring EEG and ECG in Music Listening: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review examined 18 peer-reviewed studies using simultaneous EEG and ECG during passive music listening in healthy adults. Findings were heterogeneous and lacked integration, highlighting methodological inconsistencies and a need for standardized guidelines to study brain-heart interactions in music.

papers.title: Beyond flickering: introducing code-modulated motion visual evoked potentials for brain-computer interfacing.
papers.summary: This study introduced a code-modulated motion visual evoked potential (c-MVEP) BCI paradigm and compared it to c-VEP, SSMVEP, and SSVEP, finding that c-MVEP achieved 85.67% accuracy and 2.61 s selection time in an online four-target BCI, providing a non-flickering alternative with comparable user comfort.

papers.title: SIK3 isoforms and PKA phosphorylation sites differentially regulate sleep and circadian rhythms.
papers.summary: Using isoform-selective knock-in mice, this study demonstrated that the 150 kDa SIK3 isoform regulates wakefulness at dark onset and circadian period, while the 70 kDa isoform affects NREM sleep delta power; PKA phosphorylation sites T469 and S551 mediate Sleepy-like hypersomnia phenotypes.

papers.title: Psilocybin-induced changes in electroencephalography link acute and long-term effects.
papers.summary: In a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial, psilocybin acutely reduced alpha/beta power and increased gamma diversity, returning to baseline by 6 hours. At 24 hours, reduced delta/theta power correlated with positive life changes at 4 weeks, independent of acute psychological effects.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Functional Network Responses to Immersive Virtual Reality in Alzheimer Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Exploratory Single-Session 3-Group Repeated-Measures Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study examined EEG functional network changes during immersive VR exposure in 60 older adults with Alzheimer disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal cognition. It found higher global efficiency and modularity in AD at baseline, but no significant differences during VR, suggesting state-dependent network modulation.

papers.title: Worry undermines savoring's ability to reduce negative picture processing.
papers.summary: An EEG study (N=36) found that savoring positive pictures reduced late positive potentials (LPPs) to subsequently presented negative pictures, but this effect was attenuated in individuals with higher worry levels, who showed larger LPPs to negative pictures after savoring. Self-reported pleasantness ratings were unaffected.

papers.title: Sex-dependent cortical responses to terpene-based olfactory stimulation revealed by EEG and sLORETA.
papers.summary: This study investigated cortical responses to terpene-based aromas (orange and pine) using EEG and sLORETA in males and females. It found sex-dependent changes: orange increased beta/gamma power in males, whereas pine increased beta power in females, with distinct cortical activation patterns.

papers.title: Electrophysiological Profile and Comparative Analysis in Brachial Plexus Injuries.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
papers.summary: A retrospective observational study of 78 patients with brachial plexopathy found that pan-plexopathy and upper trunk involvement were most common, and EMG provided additional diagnostic yield beyond NCS, especially for proximal and preganglionic lesions. Preganglionic and root avulsion patterns were exclusive to traumatic cases.

papers.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined With Electroencephalography Analysis Suggest Time-Dependent and Region-Specific Modulation of Cortical Excitability During Acute Alcohol Intoxication.
papers.summary: This exploratory study assessed cortical excitability changes during acute alcohol intoxication using TMS-EEG in 34 adults. Amplitude of TMS-evoked potentials (P30, N45, P60, P180, N100) decreased at 30 min and partially recovered by 120 min, with regional specificity in frontal and central regions.

papers.title: EEG Analysis of Visual Attention Under Perception of Affective Prosody in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG theta/beta ratio during visual attention tasks with affective prosody in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and typically developing controls. ASD group had higher TBR overall, and temporal TBR differed between happy and sad prosody under high load, suggesting emotion-cognition interactions.

papers.title: GCaMP fiber photometry reveals mechanistic insights into focused ultrasound neuromodulation in acute seizures.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of acute seizures, low-intensity focused ultrasound (FUS) attenuated epileptic calcium transients and ECoG spikes for up to 40 minutes, with reduced c-Fos expression co-localized with NMDAR2B and GAD65/67. These findings suggest FUS exerts calcium-dependent anti-seizure effects by modulating excitatory-inhibitory balance, with GCaMP fiber photometry as a mechanistic surrogate.

papers.title: A novel method for obtaining epileptic brain tissue for omic analyses using electrodes from a clinical stereoelectroencephalography study
papers.summary: This study describes a method to extract brain tissue from stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) electrodes for transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. Using samples from six epilepsy patients, they obtained high-quality RNA and protein and found inflammatory markers most pronounced in the epileptogenic zone.

papers.title: Non-convulsive status epilepticus revealing acute deterioration in AARS2 mutation-associated progressive leukoencephalopathy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 41-year-old woman with AARS2 mutation-associated progressive leukoencephalopathy who presented with non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) as the cause of acute clinical deterioration. EEG showed rhythmic frontal delta activity with sharp waves, and response to antiseizure treatment confirmed NCSE, highlighting the importance of considering NCSE in such patients with subacute neurological worsening.

papers.title: Feasibility of heart rate monitoring in hemodialysis patients using visible imaging: a pilot study.
papers.summary: The authors propose a remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) framework using visible imaging for continuous heart rate monitoring in hemodialysis patients. In a pilot study with eight stage-5 chronic kidney disease patients, the method achieved a mean absolute error of 1.16 beats per minute compared to ECG, demonstrating feasibility for noncontact monitoring.

papers.title: Chronic social instability stress differentially affects the behavior and the transcriptome of the anterodorsal bed nucleus of the stria terminalis between male and female mice
keywords: bed nucleus of the stria terminalis
papers.summary: Chronic social instability stress in mice caused opposite behavioral effects in males (more avoidant) and females (less avoidant), with sex-specific transcriptomic changes in the anterodorsal BNST and altered CRH neuron properties only in males.

papers.title: Impact of the Western China epilepsy initiative on epilepsy care capacity in underserved regions: a nationwide cross-sectional survey.
authors: Western China Epilepsy Initiative of the Youth Commission of the China Association Against Epilepsy
papers.summary: A nationwide cross-sectional survey of 115 hospitals and 96 experts found that the Western China Epilepsy Initiative was associated with significant post-intervention acceleration in EEG technician certifications, epileptologist certifications, and epilepsy patient visits, as well as a decline in unauthorized therapies in 87.8% of hospitals.

papers.title: Temporal variability of tryptophan-like fluorescence as a surrogate for microbial contamination and its association with flow components of karst spring discharge.
papers.summary: A 12-month high-frequency study at a karst spring in western Ireland found that tryptophan-like fluorescence variability was more strongly associated with intermediate and fast flow components than slow/baseflow, and correlated with E. coli abundance, supporting its use as a surrogate for microbial contamination.

papers.title: Electrical Signatures of Life: A Review of Cell Electrophysiology and Dielectric Analysis (2015-2026).
papers.summary: This review covers 2015-2026 literature on cell electrophysiology and dielectric analysis, focusing on label-free cellular electrical signatures (e.g., membrane capacitance, polarizability) and their applications in clinical diagnosis, drug development, and bioprocessing.

papers.title: Shielding the First 24 Postnatal Months of Life: A Proposal for a Prospective Cohort Study of Early-Life Electromagnetic Exposure and Autism Risk.
papers.summary: This protocol proposes a prospective cohort study to test whether reducing electromagnetic radiation exposure during the first 24 postnatal months, via sleep-phase Faraday shielding, can reduce autism risk, with exploratory genomic and EEG endpoints.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
